- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or is weak (negative sentiment → model underreacts).
- Model exhibits lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip faster than forecast.
- Forecast tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment swings sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high in strong uptrends and too low in strong downtrends.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the period, then converge toward true values later.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often defaults to historical mean, missing structural shifts.
- Overshoots after spikes are more common in the first 10–15 days of forecast horizon; correct by reducing slope after spike.
